The fund is a "fund of funds" investing at least 80% of its net assets in the underlying index.

title: U.S. Venture Acquires Breakthrough Fuel
summary: U.S. Venture acquired Breakthrough Fuel in 2019 for an undisclosed sum. Both companies are based in Wisconsin. The acquisition aligns with U.S. Venture's strategy to diversify its business. Breakthrough Fuel, founded in 2004, highlighted flaws in the industry-standard method for settling diesel fuel reimbursements between shippers and carriers. It argued that actual fuel prices and consumption are influenced by factors such as terrain, time, local taxes, and varying local prices, leading to discrepancies between the national average and granular data. Breakthrough Fuel reported that in 2018, an average 10 million gallon customer achieved a 53 percent reduction in intermodal fuel spend, a 570,000 gallon reduction in consumption, over 5,800 metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions avoided, and a 19 percent reduction in truckload fuel spend. U.S. Venture stated that Breakthrough helped its clients eliminate more than 8.9 million gallons of diesel fuel from their supply chains and reduce their collective carbon footprint by more than 90,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide.

summary: Schweitzer-Mauduit International, Inc. completed its acquisition of Scapa Group plc on April 15, 2021, following the effectiveness of the scheme of arrangement under the United Kingdom Companies Act 2006. The transaction involved a recommended cash offer of £2.15 per ordinary share, valuing Scapa's entire ordinary share capital at approximately £412.6 million. The acquisition was financed using proceeds from a $350.0 million Term Loan B facility and up to $325.0 million from its revolving line of credit. The company expects to settle the offer consideration by April 29, 2021. The financial details of the acquired business will be filed within 71 calendar days of the report's filing date. The merger expands its portfolio of precision engineered performance materials and enhances its innovation, design, and formulation capabilities. title: DBRS Morningstar's Takeaways from Its 2022 Credit Outlook Series: How We Rate Corporate Hybrid Instruments
summary: DBRS Morningstar published insights from its 2022 Credit Outlook series, focusing on the rating criteria for corporate hybrid instruments. Michael R. Rao, CFA, outlined that hybrid securities, which combine debt and equity features, have grown faster than preferred shares. The market now offers a wide range of hybrid instruments with new versions emerging periodically. These instruments attract different participants for various reasons. DBRS Morningstar highlights that companies issue hybrid securities to gain equity treatment from rating agencies without diluting common shareholder ownership and debt treatment from tax authorities, allowing interest expenses to be tax-deductible. The firm assigns equity weightings to hybrid securities, ranging from 0% to 100%, based on their equity-like characteristics, with the most common weighting at 50%. Its two-stage process combines primary and additional factors to determine equity weighting and caps the combined equity treatment assigned to preferred shares and hybrid securities at 10% of total capital.
